title: Where do Virahanka Fibonacci numbers lead in bigger pyramids?
description: A pyramid with four rows has the first four Virahanka Fibonacci numbers at the bottom, and one with twenty nine rows has the first twenty nine. Each row moves two places along the sequence, which gives the top of both.
teaching_notes: One idea: two neighbours in the sequence add to the number two places on, so every row of the pyramid is a run of sequence numbers two places further along. Watch for students who count the steps up as the number of rows.

video_script.why: The child builds a four row pyramid from the first four Virahanka Fibonacci numbers, sees each row move two places along, and uses that for a pyramid with twenty nine rows.
video_script.substitution: Fill the four row pyramid, then count how many places along the sequence each row moves.
video_script.anchor: a sequence strip 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21 and the two pyramids, four rows and twenty nine rows
video_script.payoff_line: The first top is twenty one, and the second top is the fifty seventh number.

final_answer.value: (i) all are Virahanka-Fibonacci numbers and the top is 21; (ii) all are Virahanka-Fibonacci numbers and the top is the 57th number
final_answer.spoken: in both pyramids all are sequence numbers. The first top is twenty one, and the second top is the fifty seventh number

maths_rules: (i) Bottom 1, 2, 3, 5; next row 3, 5, 8; next row 8, 13; top 8 + 13 = 21, the 7th number.
Two neighbours add to the number two places on, so each row starts two places further along than the row below.
(ii) 29 rows: the top is 28 steps up, so it is at place 1 + 2 x 28 = 57, the 57th number.
video_script.design: One idea: each row moves two places along the sequence. The sequence strip stays in the anchor band and each pyramid sits on the working board.
